rule.name: LocalExecutorNeverShutDown
rule.message: This fixed thread pool is created in a local variable, and the method never shuts it down, returns it, stores it or hands it to another method. The worker threads of a fixed pool are not daemon threads and never time out, so they stay alive after the method returns and every call leaks a pool of threads until the process runs out of them. Create the pool once and share it (a field, or an injected bean that Spring shuts down), or shut it down here: try-with-resources on Java 19 and later (the pool is an AutoCloseable there), or pool.shutdown() in a finally block. An exception fits a pool that a callback shuts down later, which this rule cannot see.
